description: Mitigations for caught-in/between and machinery entanglement. Guarding and LOTO are the dominant controls. The key question: does the machine stop when it meets a human body?

mitigations.name: guarding_by_design
mitigations.description: Machine designed with integral guarding that cannot be removed without tools. EN ISO 12100 risk reduction by design. Nip points and rotating parts enclosed as part of the machine structure.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.01. Can't be casually defeated. Failure: guard design doesn't cover all access points, maintenance access allows bypass.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: If nip points are enclosed, entanglement cannot occur during normal operation. Maintenance access is the residual gap.

mitigations.name: fixed_guard
mitigations.description: Fixed guard panels requiring tools to remove. EN 953. Prevents access to nip points and rotating parts during operation.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.03. Failure: guard removed for cleaning/adjustment and not replaced, guard damaged, bolts missing allowing removal without tools.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When in place, prevents body access to danger zone. Very high effectiveness. PUWER Reg 11.

mitigations.name: interlocked_guard
mitigations.description: Guard with interlock switch — opening the guard stops the machine. EN ISO 14119. Allows access for cleaning/adjustment while ensuring machine is stopped.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.04. Failure: interlock defeated/bypassed (common — tied off, magnet), run-down time allows access before machine stops, interlock wiring fault.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When working, machine stops before guard fully opens. Effectiveness limited by machine run-down time (high-inertia machines keep rotating after power cut).

mitigations.name: light_curtain
mitigations.description: Electro-sensitive protective equipment (ESPE) — light curtain or laser scanner detects body part entering danger zone and stops machine. EN 61496.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Failure: muting for material feed, blanking for small parts, contaminated optics, response time exceeds stopping time.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Stops machine when beam is broken. Effectiveness depends on response time vs approach speed. Not suitable for machines with long run-down times.

mitigations.name: loto_machinery
mitigations.description: Lockout/Tagout during maintenance, cleaning, unjamming. Physical isolation of all energy sources (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, gravitational). The critical control for maintenance-phase caught-in.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Same as electrical LOTO. Most caught-in fatalities occur during maintenance when guards are legitimately removed and LOTO was not applied.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When all energy sources are isolated and verified, machine cannot move. Near-complete protection. The gap is stored energy (springs, elevated parts).

mitigations.name: e_stop
mitigations.description: Emergency stop button within reach of operator. Stops machine after entanglement begins. Post-impact — the injury has started, e-stop limits its duration.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Failure: button not within reach, operator incapacitated, machine has long run-down time, bystander doesn't know which button.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Reduces the duration of entanglement. For high-torque machines, damage occurs in fractions of a second — e-stop may be too slow. Most effective for low-torque machines that can be stopped before full draw-in.
